jei.jasm.info.capacity_wafer.1: Stores items for a Deck. It holds any mix of items, up to its capacity.
jei.jasm.info.capacity_wafer.2: Link it to an Archive: if the wafer is ever lost or destroyed, the Archive can bring it back onto a blank wafer of equal or larger capacity.
jei.jasm.info.capacity_wafer.3: Three wafers of one size, crafted together, make the next size and keep everything inside.
jei.jasm.info.type_wafer.1: Stores a few kinds of items in large amounts. Each kind is a type; items that don't stack count as a type each.
jei.jasm.info.type_wafer.2: Link it to an Archive to be able to recover it.
jei.jasm.info.type_wafer.3: Two Type Wafers of one size, crafted together, make the next size and keep everything inside.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_capacity_wafer.1: Stores fluids for a Deck. It holds any mix of fluids, up to its capacity in buckets.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_capacity_wafer.2: Link it to an Archive to be able to recover it onto a blank fluid wafer of equal or larger capacity.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_capacity_wafer.3: Three wafers of one size, crafted together, make the next size and keep everything inside.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_type_wafer.1: Stores a few kinds of fluid in large amounts. Each fluid is a type.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_type_wafer.2: Link it to an Archive to be able to recover it.
jei.jasm.info.fluid_type_wafer.3: Two Type Fluid Wafers of one size, crafted together, make the next size and keep everything inside.
jei.jasm.info.deck.1: Portable storage. Put wafers in the side panel, then store and take items through the grid.
jei.jasm.info.deck.2: A Deck uses power while it is open. Charge it in a Combustion Generator or anything else that charges items.
jei.jasm.info.deck.3: Right-click a wafer in the side panel to set its priority and filter.
jei.jasm.info.crafting_deck.1: A Deck with a crafting grid. Ingredients come straight from its wafers, and the grid refills itself after each craft.
jei.jasm.info.crafting_deck.2: Shift-click the result to craft as many as fit in your inventory. When you close it, the grid goes back into the wafers.
jei.jasm.info.crafting_deck.3: Made from a Deck of the same tier, keeping its wafers and charge.
jei.jasm.info.recipe_card.1: Holds one crafting recipe for autocrafting. Write it at an Encoding Terminal: set the recipe in the grid, put an Empty or Filled card in, and press Encode.
jei.jasm.info.recipe_card.2: A Filled card alone in a crafting grid turns back into an Empty one.
jei.jasm.info.encoding_terminal.1: Writes recipes onto Recipe Cards. Click items into its grid: they are only examples and are never used up.
jei.jasm.info.encoding_terminal.2: It pairs one Deck per player with its network. Open the Deck Link window with the side key, put a Deck in its left slot, then take it from the right. Pairing another replaces that player's previous Deck. Trusted players share recipes but use their own stored items. It needs power.
jei.jasm.info.recipe_rack.1: Holds 16 Filled Recipe Cards. Every Crafting Server on the same network can use them.
jei.jasm.info.recipe_rack.2: It needs power: without it, the network can't see its cards.
jei.jasm.info.data_cable.1: Joins crafting blocks into one network, and carries power between them from anything that makes it.
jei.jasm.info.data_cable.2: Any two cables join. Cables hold no power and have no speed limit: what a generator or Power Acceptor pushes in goes straight to the machines on the network that need it, and a source with nothing to feed keeps its power. Machines only get power through a cable, or from a generator or Power Acceptor they touch.
jei.jasm.info.crafting_server.1: Runs one crafting job at a time. Processors decide how many crafts run at once; Storage Modules how big a job fits.
jei.jasm.info.crafting_server.2: Its parts are locked in while it works. Broken, it spills whatever its job held.
jei.jasm.info.processor.1: Goes in a Crafting Server. Each tier runs four times the crafts of the tier below, at the same speed.
jei.jasm.info.storage_module.1: Goes in a Crafting Server: room for a job's ingredients and everything it makes along the way.
jei.jasm.info.archive.1: Protects the wafers linked to it. If a linked wafer is lost, the Archive can recover it, items and all, onto a blank wafer. Shift-right-click with its linked Deck to back up wafers in slot order, up to the Archive's free registrations. Wafers already backed up on the same network are skipped. The message counts all backed-up wafers in the Deck, including earlier backups.
jei.jasm.info.archive.2: A standalone Archive lets its owner back up and recover wafers without an Encoding Terminal or paired Deck. On a network it defaults to the network owner. The owner can use its Deck link slots to select another trusted player's paired Deck instead. Only the selected player can back up or recover wafers; trusted players may view. Changing to another player or network clears the backups. Losing or replacing a Deck for the same player preserves backups. Linking and recovery need power.
jei.jasm.info.combustion_generator.1: Burns anything a furnace burns to make power, and sends it into the blocks it touches. Items that store power charge in its charging slot.
jei.jasm.info.combustion_generator.2: Higher tiers burn fuel faster and make more power from it.

screen.jasm.storage.priority_hint: Higher priority takes items and fluids in first. The lowest is emptied first.
screen.jasm.transfer.redstone_hint: Click to change mode. Controls both input and output.
jei.jasm.info.redstone_upgrade.1: Install one in an Input, Output or Input Output Port's upgrade slots. Its mode button chooses whether to ignore redstone, run while powered or run while unpowered. The mode controls both transfer directions. Removing the upgrade restores normal operation.
jei.jasm.info.redstone_upgrade.2: All ports in the same block space receive the same redstone signal. Each upgraded port follows its own mode; ports without a Redstone Upgrade keep running normally. Access Ports do not accept this upgrade.

screen.jasm.server.processors_hint: Each Processor runs one craft at a time, or keeps one set out in a machine until its results come back. With all of them busy, the job waits even if other machines are free: add Processors to use more machines at once.
jei.jasm.info.access_port.1: Place it next to furnaces or any other machines, and join it to the network with a Data Cable. Every block touching it that takes items is a machine you can write processing cards for.
jei.jasm.info.access_port.2: The results must come back into the port: set the machine to output into it, or use a hopper or pipe.

jei.jasm.info.crystal_seed.1: Use a Crystal Seed on a Block of Amethyst to turn it into Seeded Amethyst.
jei.jasm.info.crystal_seed.2: Seeded Amethyst grows Data Crystal buds on its free sides. A full Data Crystal Cluster drops Data Crystals; Fortune gives more. Buds broken early drop Crystal Dust.
jei.jasm.info.crystal_seed.3: Each time a bud grows, the block may wear down: Seeded, then Worn, then Cracked, then back to a plain Block of Amethyst. Mined at any stage, it drops a Block of Amethyst and the seed is lost.
jei.jasm.info.data_crystal.1: Mined from a full Data Crystal Cluster, which grows on Seeded Amethyst. Fortune gives more.
jei.jasm.info.data_crystal.2: Cut one into a Blank Chip at a Stonecutter. Four make a Wrench. A wild Bitling will follow you for a while if you hand it one.
jei.jasm.info.crystal_resonator.1: Place it touching Seeded Amethyst and give it power, from a Data Cable or a generator. Every Seeded Amethyst it touches grows faster, and several Resonators on one block add up.
jei.jasm.info.crystal_resonator.2: Without power it does nothing. Each Resonator takes up one side of the block, so that side can't grow. Its extra growth wears the block down more gently than natural growth, so a seed gives more crystals in total, and much sooner.
jei.jasm.info.bitling.1: Bitlings are little helpers that work the Chip Workshop. A Basic Bitling makes all three chip types. Craft it with chips of one type to get a Logic, Memory or Link Bitling, which mostly makes its own type.
jei.jasm.info.bitling.2: A Logic, Memory or Link Bitling or Nibbling learns from every chip it makes. With a full training bar it can evolve in a crafting grid: Bitling, then Nibbling, then Byteling. Each stage makes better chips and has a bigger battery.
jei.jasm.info.bitling.3: Each critter carries its own battery. When it runs flat it takes a nap in the Workshop until it is charged again.

screen.jasm.bay.status.obstructed: Something is standing in the way

screen.jasm.workshop.no_critter: Put a Bitling in the slot to start.
screen.jasm.workshop.napping: Zzz… wake me when I'm full.
jei.jasm.info.chip_workshop.1: A Bitling in the Workshop turns Blank Chips into Logic, Memory and Link Chips, and now and then an Advanced one. Without a Bitling nothing happens.
jei.jasm.info.chip_workshop.2: Single makes one chip at a time. Batch makes multiple per process. Every chip costs uses charge from the Bitling's battery. Power from a cable or a generator next to it charges that battery.
screen.jasm.workshop.no_recipe_line: I don't know what to make with these.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.1: One, two, three... one, two, three. Yep, still three.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.2: Every chip gets checked twice. Twice! That's the rule.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.3: Zero mistakes so far. I counted. Twice.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.4: This one was a little crooked. There. Much better.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.6: Chip number... hold on, let me count again.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.7: Measure twice, cut once. Then measure again.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.8: Logic Chip, Logic Chip, Logic Chip. Lovely.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.9: Neat little rows, just the way I like them.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.work.10: I like it when things add up.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.1: I sorted your chips by colour. Then by size. Then by colour again.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.2: I made a list of my lists.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.3: If a chip is blank, is it really a chip? I think about this a lot.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.4: Logic says more Blank Chips would be nice.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.5: Nothing to do. I've tidied the bench four times.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.6: I've counted the rivets on this Workshop. There are 112.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.7: Waiting is just counting very slowly.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.8: I could make chips, if someone brought me Blank ones.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.9: Everything is in order. Suspiciously in order.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.logic.idle.10: Hm. A spare moment. Let me recount the output.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.1: Mine. This one's mine. They're all mine, really.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.2: *yawn* I remember every chip I ever made.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.3: One for you... one for my pile... one for you...
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.4: I keep a spare. And a spare for the spare.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.5: Don't take the shiny ones. I'm saving those.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.7: This chip goes on the good pile.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.8: I'll remember this one. I remember all of them.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.9: Mmm... what was I doing? Oh right. Chips.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.work.10: Warm chips, fresh off the bench. Cosy.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.1: This pile is my pillow now.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.3: I dreamt about chips. Then I woke up and made some.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.4: Remember that one chip? I do. It was lovely.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.5: Cosy. Warm. Surrounded by chips. Perfect.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.6: No chips to make? More time to count my collection.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.7: I could sleep here. I think I will.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.8: Quiet days are the best for hoarding.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.memory.idle.10: Wake me when there's something to keep.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.1: Chip for you, chip for you, chips for everyone!
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.3: Pass it on! No really, pass it on.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.4: Busy busy busy! Messages don't carry themselves.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.5: This one's got a note stuck to it. Oops.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.7: The cables are buzzing today. Everyone wants chips!
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.8: Tell the hopper I'll be right with it.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.9: Another one for the network. They love these.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.work.10: I'll let the Crafting Server know. It'll be thrilled.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.2: Did you hear? The furnace next door is running hot again.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.3: I've got a note for you! ...I forgot what it says.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.4: The cables tell me everything. Everything!
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.5: Have you met the Crafting Server? Lovely, but always so busy.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.6: I told the chest about you. It was very impressed.
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.7: Ooh, a visitor! Stay and chat?
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.8: Quiet today. Too quiet. Say something!
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.9: No chips? Then let's talk. How's your day?
screen.jasm.workshop.line.link.idle.10: I heard a rumour about a Byteling. Want to hear it?
jei.jasm.info.crystal_foundry.1: Grows Data Crystals from Crystal Seeds and cuts each one straight into a Blank Chip. Every seed always makes the same number of chips, more than a Seeded Amethyst gives on average.
jei.jasm.info.crystal_foundry.2: It needs power while it grows. A seed is used up as soon as it starts. Hoppers and pipes can feed seeds in and take Blank Chips out.
screen.jasm.brain.status.resting: Resting: another brain leads this network
screen.jasm.brain.use.tower: The whole tower uses this, and shares one pool of power
jade.jasm.chamber.alone: Not part of a brain floor
jei.jasm.info.network_brain.1: A network without a Network Brain can hold %s machines. With more, the whole network stops until you add a brain or remove a machine. Ports, Archives and JASM machines joined by cable or by touching each other count; cables, generators, Creative Batteries, brains and chambers don't. A lone brain with power lets the network hold %s.
jei.jasm.info.network_brain.2: Put 8 Network Chambers round a brain, on its layer, to make a brain floor, which lets the network hold %s machines. Stack floors straight on top of each other into a tower, each with its own brain. A cable on any block of the tower powers all of it. When a network holds several brains or towers, only the one with the most floors leads.
jei.jasm.info.network_chamber.1: Place 8 round a Network Brain, on the same layer, to make a brain floor. Cables can join any block of the floor, and right-clicking a chamber opens its brain's screen.
jei.jasm.info.basic_bitling.1: Found in the wild on grassy land, and drawn to growing Data Crystals.
jei.jasm.info.basic_bitling.2: Give one a Logic, Memory or Link Chip to befriend it. Give it a Data Crystal and it follows you for a while.
jei.jasm.info.bitling_station.1: Put a Bitling, Nibbling or Byteling in the station and a little living Bitling pops out and roams around it, running, hopping, looking around and lying down for a rest. You can pet it.
jei.jasm.info.bitling_station.2: Roaming uses the Bitling's own battery. When it runs low the Bitling walks home and charges on the pad from the station's power, so connect it to a Data Cable network or put a generator next to it. If it is knocked out it comes back after a short wait.
